summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of kidney and pancreas transplants, type 1 diabetes, and chronic heart failure was admitted for right leg cellulitis and a non-occlusive popliteal vein thrombus. She was started on vancomycin and heparin. During the hospitalization, she developed worsening pulmonary edema and respiratory distress requiring ICU admission and BiPAP support. Her condition improved with hemodialysis and ultrafiltration. She also experienced atrial fibrillation with tachycardia, managed with amiodarone and anticoagulation with warfarin. Repeat imaging showed no DVT, and the final diagnosis was cellulitis without thrombosis. Blood cultures remained negative, and antibiotics were discontinued. She completed a course of meropenem and was transitioned to oral medications. Her immunosuppressants were adjusted, and she was discharged to extended care in stable condition with instructions for CPAP use, daily weight monitoring, and close follow-up.
